risks.title: Deterioration of Local Economic Conditions
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in the summary and detailed in the 'Risks Related to Economic Conditions and Operating Environment' section. The intensity of language is high ('materially adversely affect') and the context emphasizes the company's geographic concentration. The weighting of the Macro category is high.

risks.title: Increased Competition from Banks and Fintechs
risks.score_rationale: Strongly emphasized in 'Risks Related to Competition and Reputation' with an extensive list of competitors (banks, credit unions, fintechs, stablecoins). The language is intense ('very competitive', 'substantially greater resources'). The focus on technology and new regulations (GENIUS Act) indicates an upward trend in this risk.

risks.title: Climate Change Risks
risks.score_rationale: Presented in 'Risks Related to Economic Conditions and Operating Environment' with detailed description of physical and transition risks. The language is measured but the subject is novel and complex. The Macro category is relevant.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and Information Security Risks
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in 'Risks Related to General Operations' and 'Risks Related to Competition and Reputation' as a potential source of reputational damage and losses. The intensity of language is measured ('fraud and security risks', 'cyber-attacks', 'information security breaches'). This risk is pervasive in the financial sector.

risks.title: Regulatory and Compliance Risks
risks.score_rationale: Detailed in 'Legal and Regulatory Risks' with a lengthy list of potential regulations (capital ratios, monetary policy, consumer protection laws, etc.). The language is strong ('increased regulatory rigor', 'heightened capital'). The nature of the banking sector makes this risk permanent and potentially evolving.

risks.title: Credit and Loan Loss Risks
risks.score_rationale: Central in 'Risks Related to Lending Operations' and mentioned in the economic context. The focus is on the sufficiency of allowance for credit losses and dependence on borrower viability. The language is direct ('sufficiency to absorb losses', 'increase in loan charge-offs'). This is a fundamental risk for a bank.

risks.title: Reputational Damage
risks.score_rationale: Prominently featured in 'Risks Related to Competition and Reputation' as a major risk ('damage to our reputation may harm our business', 'critical to our ability to attract and maintain customers'). Sources are multiple (professional misconduct, cyber-attacks, litigation). Rapid dissemination via social media amplifies this risk.
